name: Savanto – AI Search & Chat
author: intufind

sections.description:
A visitor searches your site for “comfortable shoes for hiking” and gets nothing back. WordPress search matches words, not meaning, so anything phrased differently to your product titles returns an empty page.

Savanto replaces that search. It understands what people are asking for, adds a chat assistant that answers from your own content, and suggests related products. You do not need an OpenAI account, an API key, or any technical setup.

Install the plugin, activate it, and click Connect to Savanto. You sign in or create a free account, approve the connection, and your site is live. There is no key to copy. Savanto runs the AI on its own servers, so you never manage tokens, usage limits, or billing with OpenAI, Anthropic, or anyone else.

How Savanto Differs From Other AI Plugins

Most WordPress AI plugins are toolkits. They connect your site to an external AI provider, but you bring your own API key, configure embeddings, choose models, and build the experience yourself. That suits developers. It does not suit a store owner who wants better search.

Savanto is a finished product rather than a toolkit. There is no API key from OpenAI, Anthropic or Google to supply, no third-party AI account to manage, no vector database to stand up, and no prompts or models to choose. Everything runs on Savanto’s own infrastructure, so there are no usage bills arriving from providers you did not sign up with.

Savanto uses different models for different jobs, each chosen and tuned for the task: ranking search results, holding a conversation, matching products. You get that work without configuring any of it.

Other AI plugins need your own keys and some developer knowledge before they do anything. Some support platforms sell AI as an add-on from around $29 a month. Savanto gives you search and chat on a free plan that does not expire, with nothing else to set up. Paid plans start at $9 a month when you need higher limits.

Semantic Search

Replaces WordPress search with search that reads intent. Someone types “something warm but not too bulky” or “gifts under $50 for someone who likes cooking” and gets sensible results. Typos, vague descriptions and full questions all work without tuning.

Chat Assistant

An assistant on your site that answers questions from the content you have synced, suggests products, and points people to the right page. It works from your own material, so it is not guessing at what you sell.

Recommendations

Suggestions drawn from what a visitor is actually looking for, rather than from cookies or browsing history. Related products, posts and pages that a category-based list would have missed.

Live Agent Handoff

The assistant recognises a question it should not answer alone and hands the visitor to your support team, so nobody reaches a dead end.

Automatic Sync

Publish a page, product or post and Savanto picks it up. Nothing to re-index by hand, and search results stay current as your content changes.

Built for WooCommerce

Savanto reads your whole catalogue: titles, descriptions, prices, categories and custom fields. Visitors search in their own words and still find the right product, which means fewer searches that end in nothing.

Privacy

Savanto indexes only publicly available content. It does not touch private posts, drafts, user accounts or personal data.

Performance

Search runs on Savanto’s infrastructure with global edge delivery, so it adds no load to your WordPress hosting. Responses typically return in under 100ms. Enterprise plans include a contractual uptime SLA with service credits.

Compatible With

  • WordPress
  • WooCommerce
  • Elementor
  • Gutenberg
  • Advanced Custom Fields (ACF)

Developer API available at savanto.ai/docs/api for custom integrations.

Getting Started

Install the plugin, activate it, and click Connect to Savanto. You are live once you have signed in and approved the connection, and Savanto begins indexing your content. Most sites are fully searchable within minutes.

Guides for installation, search, chat, recommendations and troubleshooting are at savanto.ai/docs/wordpress.

The free plan needs no credit card and does not expire. Paid plans start at $9 a month.

Use of Third Party Services

This plugin connects to Savanto’s servers to provide its search and chat features. When activated, your publicly available site content (pages, posts, and products) is sent to Savanto’s servers for indexing and processing.

  • Savanto – Terms of Service | Privacy Policy

No data is shared with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any other third party AI provider. All AI processing is handled through Savanto’s own infrastructure.

Privacy

This plugin connects to the Savanto cloud service (savanto.ai) to provide its search and chat features.

Data Sent to Savanto

When you connect and sync content, the following data is transmitted to Savanto servers:

  • Post and page content (title, body, excerpt, permalink)
  • Product information for WooCommerce (name, description, price, SKU, categories, images)
  • Taxonomy terms (categories, tags, product attributes)
  • Post meta that is marked as public

Data NOT Collected

  • User personal information (emails, names, addresses)
  • Order details or customer data
  • Passwords or authentication credentials
  • Private or draft content (only published content is synced)
  • Comments or user-generated content

Chat Widget

The chat widget loads from Savanto’s CDN (cdn.savanto.ai). When visitors use the chat:

  • Their questions are processed by Savanto’s AI
  • No personally identifiable information is collected
  • Chat conversations are not stored unless you enable analytics in your dashboard

MCP Server (WooCommerce)

If you enable the MCP Orders domain for WooCommerce:

  • Order lookups are performed locally on your WordPress server
  • Order data stays on your server and is not sent to Savanto
  • The Savanto cloud only routes requests to your server

How Order Lookups Work:

When a customer asks about their orders through the chat:

  1. The question is analyzed by Savanto’s AI in the cloud
  2. If it’s an order question, Savanto sends a request back to YOUR WordPress site
  3. Your WordPress plugin looks up the order using WooCommerce
  4. Only the relevant order summary is returned to complete the AI response

The full order database is never accessed by or copied to Savanto servers.

Data Retention

  • Synced content remains in Savanto’s cloud until you disconnect or delete it
  • Disconnecting removes all your indexed content from Savanto servers
  • You can request complete data deletion by contacting support@savanto.ai

External Service

This plugin connects to the Savanto cloud service to provide its search and chat features. The plugin and cloud service are developed by the same team. By using this plugin, you agree to Savanto’s:

  • Terms of Service
  • Privacy Policy

GDPR Compliance

Savanto is designed with privacy in mind. Since no personal user data is collected or transmitted, standard GDPR consent mechanisms for visitor data are not required. However, you should update your site’s privacy policy to disclose that content is processed by a third-party AI service.
sections.installation:
Automatic Installation

  1. Log in to your WordPress admin dashboard
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New
  3. Search for “Savanto”
  4. Click Install Now and then Activate
  5. Go to Savanto → Settings and click Connect to Savanto

Manual Installation

  1. Download the plugin ZIP file
  2. Go to Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin
  3. Upload the ZIP file and click Install Now
  4. Activate the plugin
  5. Go to Savanto → Settings and click Connect to Savanto

Connecting Your Site

Click Connect to Savanto on the Settings screen. You are taken to savanto.ai to sign in or create a free account, you approve the connection, and you land back in WordPress connected. Your content starts syncing on its own.

Connecting With a Secret Key Instead

If you would rather not use the guided flow, or you are moving a site between accounts:

  1. Create a free account at savanto.ai
  2. Create a workspace for your site
  3. Copy your Secret Key from the workspace settings
  4. On the Settings screen, expand Use a secret key instead and paste it

No third-party API keys required either way. Savanto handles all AI processing on its own infrastructure.
sections.faq:
Do I need an OpenAI or ChatGPT API key?

No. Savanto runs on its own AI infrastructure. You do not need an account or API key from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, or any other AI provider. Everything is included.

How long does setup take?

Under a minute. Install the plugin, activate it, and click Connect to Savanto. Signing in or creating an account takes care of the rest, and Savanto starts indexing your site automatically. Most sites are fully searchable within a few minutes.

Do I need WooCommerce?

No. Savanto works with any WordPress site. WooCommerce adds product sync, product recommendations, and an Orders domain so the assistant can answer questions about orders.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes. Savanto indexes your full product catalog including titles, descriptions, pricing, categories, custom fields, and metadata. It’s built with ecommerce in mind.

Will this slow down my site?

No. Savanto runs on external servers with global edge deployment. It does not add processing load to your WordPress hosting. Response times are under 100ms.

What content does Savanto index?

Savanto indexes publicly available pages, posts, and products on your site. You can configure which post types to sync. It never touches private content, drafts, user accounts, or personal information.

Does the AI chat assistant make things up?

Savanto’s chat assistant responds based on your actual site content. It does not pull from general internet knowledge or generate responses unrelated to your site.

Can I customize the appearance?

Yes. You can customize the look and placement of both the search and chat interfaces to match your site’s branding from the Savanto Dashboard.

Does it work with page builders?

Yes. Savanto is compatible with Elementor, Gutenberg, and other popular page builders. It also supports Advanced Custom Fields.

What is MCP?

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard for AI agents to interact with external services. Savanto’s MCP server allows AI agents to query orders and perform actions in your WooCommerce store.

Is it really free?

Yes. The free plan does not expire: 1,000 searches and 50 chat messages a month, with no credit card. Your first two weeks include higher limits to help you get set up. Paid plans start at $9/month when you need more.

Is there a developer API?

Yes. Full API documentation is available at savanto.ai/docs/api for custom integrations and advanced use cases.

How is this different from other AI plugins?

Most AI plugins are developer toolkits that require your own API keys from providers like OpenAI. You configure the models, manage embeddings, and build the search or chat experience yourself. Savanto is a finished product that works immediately with no technical setup.

How is this different from live chat plugins?

Live chat plugins are customer support platforms where AI is typically a premium add-on. Savanto is an AI search and chat product from the ground up, purpose built to help visitors find what they’re looking for and convert. There is a free plan, and paid plans start at $9/month.

Is my data secure?

Yes. All communication with the Savanto cloud uses HTTPS encryption. Your Secret Key is stored securely in your WordPress database and never exposed to visitors.

What happens if I disconnect or uninstall?

When you disconnect from the Settings page, all your indexed content is deleted from Savanto’s servers and all plugin settings are removed. When you uninstall the plugin, it performs the same cleanup automatically.
sections.changelog:
1.4.13

  • Order support no longer reports an SSL failure on sites that are not yet served over HTTPS. It now says plainly that HTTPS is required and what to do about it, and stops making a request the cloud was always going to reject. “Retry Registration” honours the same rule, instead of repeating the failed call.
  • The Status screen no longer shows order support as “Registered” alongside an error saying it is not.
  • Connecting your site shows one message about what happened rather than two that disagreed: the confirmation used to say your content was syncing directly above a second notice saying the sync had finished.
  • A content sync that takes a while now says so, and keeps saying so until it reports. Previously a slow first sync gave no feedback at all.
  • The “Connect to Savanto” and “Finish setup” buttons show that they are working. Both spend a moment talking to Savanto before the page changes, and previously looked unresponsive — inviting a second click that started the work twice.
  • Fixed the Sync switch in the Posts, Pages and Products lists appearing to break while it saved. It faded to half opacity, which at that size left a pale bar with a dot on it that looked like a stray dash. It now keeps its colour while it works.

1.4.12

  • Added one-click “Connect to Savanto”: sign in or create a free account, approve the connection, and your site is connected. There is no secret key to copy from the dashboard — key entry is still available under “Use a secret key instead” if you prefer it.
  • Connecting now uses the workspace already on your account instead of failing with “Workspace limit reached”. Reconnecting the same site reuses its existing workspace rather than trying to create a duplicate.
  • The first content sync is queued in the background instead of running while you are redirected back to WordPress, so sites with large catalogs no longer time out with credentials already saved.
  • Signing up part-way through connecting has longer to finish, so the connection no longer expires while you are checking your email for the verification link.
  • A connection that fails now says why, including the response from Savanto. Previously every failure reported that the site must be served over HTTPS, which was often wrong and sent troubleshooting in the wrong direction.
  • Setup that stops before it finishes is now detected and reported on the Settings screen, with a “Finish setup” button that completes it. Previously the site showed as connected while search and chat stayed switched off and the first sync never ran.
  • Retrying a connection no longer leaves unused secret keys on your Savanto account; the previous key for the site is revoked once its replacement exists.
  • Tidied the Settings screen: one clear way to connect, secret-key entry tucked behind a disclosure, and the connected state shows status and actions separately.
  • Fixed the Savanto columns in the Posts, Pages and Products lists: the status dropdown rendered at full form-field size inside the row, and the sync switch sat slightly above it. The two columns are now labelled “Sync” and “Visibility” instead of unlabelled icons.
  • Clarified wording across the admin screens.

1.4.11

  • Reframed the AI Chat and Live Agent Handoff screenshots so they display fully in the listing gallery. No functional changes to the plugin.

1.4.10

  • Added Content Sync and Taxonomies screenshots to the listing. No functional changes to the plugin.

1.4.9

  • Removed two outdated demo videos and added a link to the WordPress setup guides. No functional changes to the plugin.

1.4.8

  • Refreshed the wordpress.org listing: updated banner, icon, and screenshots to current Savanto branding. No functional changes to the plugin.

1.4.7

  • Re-validating your API key after a typo no longer clears an already-working key — the new key is saved only after it validates successfully.
  • Search results now include synced pages and custom post types in general searches, not only blog posts; the search cache also refreshes when you change which post types are synced.
  • AI recommendation blocks now refresh correctly after a product is added, edited, or deleted.
  • Product title-only edits now re-sync to search and chat.
  • Hardened content-sync pagination against runaway loops on very large catalogs.
  • Added developer hooks (savanto_product_document filter and savanto_resync_product action) so integrations such as live/spot-price plugins can shape the indexed product document and trigger re-indexing when prices change.

1.4.6

  • Fixed real-time taxonomy sync: the background batch handler for category and tag changes was never registered, so queued term updates were dropped silently.
  • Scheduled sync now includes enabled taxonomies, not only posts and products.
  • Deactivation and disconnect clear all Savanto cron events (scheduled sync and batch processors).
  • Manual sync uses a short-lived lock so overlapping admin and cron syncs do not run at the same time.
  • Sync interval is clamped to supported values (6h–48h); invalid or zero values fall back to the default.
  • Orphan cleanup is skipped when a sync hits the plan indexing limit so valid cloud documents are not removed.

1.4.5

  • Security: removed the API key, JWT secret, publishable key, and last MCP error from WordPress’s alloptions autoload cache. Existing installs are migrated automatically on first load.
  • Hardened the admin settings, MCP wiring, and sync-status options to write with autoload=false so they aren’t re-cached on save.

1.4.4

  • Brand rename: this plugin is now Savanto. After updating you will see “Savanto – AI Search & Chat” in your plugins list, on every admin page, and in the WordPress.org listing
  • Switched the cloud API endpoint to api.savanto.ai. Existing connections continue to work — settings, API keys, and indexed content are preserved
  • Refreshed admin UI copy, links, and documentation references to point at savanto.ai
  • Internal refactor: plugin classes renamed to the Savanto_* namespace. No impact on stored settings or data

1.4.3

  • Fixed API compatibility issue where workspace-scoped endpoints returned “Workspace is undefined” after backend migration
  • Improved alert spacing consistency across Knowledge Base and other admin pages

1.4.2

  • Improved code quality and WordPress coding standards compliance across all admin templates
  • Fixed PHPStan static analysis errors for stricter type safety
  • Replaced urlencode with rawurlencode for proper URL encoding

1.4.1

  • Added WPBakery Visual Composer content extraction with base64-encoded vc_raw_html support
  • Added page builder detection on Knowledge and Status pages with contextual tip to try the web crawler
  • Improved shortcode stripping with regex fallback for unregistered shortcodes (WPBakery, Divi, Avada)

1.4.0

  • Content sync now preserves document structure (headings, lists, bold, links) as markdown for better AI search and chat quality
  • Added html_to_markdown() converter for rich content fields (post content, product descriptions, ACF WYSIWYG, Divi builder)
  • Retained plain-text extraction for short fields like excerpts and text-only ACF fields

1.3.0

  • Added FacetWP integration — FacetWP Search facets now use Savanto semantic search automatically
  • Savanto appears as a selectable search engine in FacetWP’s Search facet settings
  • Auto-intercepts FacetWP’s default WP search engine when the Savanto Search Override is enabled
  • Detects listing post types to query the correct API endpoint (posts, products, or both)
  • Added integrations directory for organized third-party plugin support

1.2.3

  • Fixed bulk sync failing entirely when batch exceeds plan indexing limit — now processes as many items as will fit
  • Added retry with exponential backoff for rate-limited API requests during bulk sync
  • Fixed error code detection for indexing limit responses
  • Fixed _hash field leaking to API in real-time sync batches

1.2.2

  • Fixed RSS feed requests and bot-like URL patterns being logged as native search queries
  • Added search term validation to filter out junk entries before they reach analytics

1.2.1

  • Fixed search shortcode not opening the modal when clicked before the widget finishes loading
  • Added graceful fallback to native site search if the widget fails to load (CDN/network issues)

1.2.0

  • Fixed $0 price display for WooCommerce variable products and products with a $0 sale price
  • Added price range display for variable products (e.g. “$89.00 – $200.00”)
  • Added separate admin toggle for the floating search trigger button (defaults to off)
  • Added admin toggle to enable/disable the search widget entirely
  • Fixed flash of unstyled content (FOUC) on the [savanto_search] shortcode
  • Added shortcode usage info and styling reference to the Search admin page

1.1.1

  • Declared compatibility with WooCommerce HPOS (High-Performance Order Storage) and block-based Cart/Checkout

1.1.0

  • Added [savanto_search] shortcode for placing an inline search trigger button anywhere on the site
  • Added savanto_search_button() template tag for theme developers
  • Four trigger variants: default, compact, icon, and bar (Spotlight-style)
  • Platform-aware keyboard shortcut badge with auto dark mode, high contrast, and reduced motion support
  • CSS custom properties for easy styling overrides
  • Improved floating search trigger accessibility (focus-visible, reduced motion, high contrast)

1.0.8

  • Fixed orphan cleanup incorrectly deleting valid cloud documents when plan indexing limit is reached during sync
  • Fixed API error handling crash on PHP 8 when error response contains non-string payloads

1.0.7

  • Fixed post type filter not being applied during orphan cleanup, preventing unintended document removal during sync

1.0.6

  • Fixed DELETE API requests to ensure the request body is sent correctly

1.0.5

  • Improved cache invalidation for content deletion to prevent stale data
  • Enhanced bulk sync actions to immediately reflect changes in the cloud
  • Added error handling for cloud deletion failures with appropriate error messages

1.0.4

  • Moved inline CSS to enqueued stylesheet per WordPress coding standards

1.0.3

  • Improved service status messaging for clearer account state communication
  • User-friendly error messages during sync operations
  • Removed internal notices from admin pages for a cleaner experience

1.0.2

  • Fixed WordPress admin notices appearing between page title and subtitle

1.0.1

  • Improved disconnected state UI with clearer service status messaging
  • Connection verification now runs for previously-connected sites
  • Warning status indicator and contextual actions (Reconnect / Manage Account / Change Key)
  • Alert dismiss button now inherits brand color

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • AI-powered semantic search for WordPress and WooCommerce
  • Automatic content sync to Savanto cloud
  • MCP server for AI agent integration (WooCommerce orders)
  • Chat widget integration with cloud-managed configuration
  • Native WordPress and WooCommerce search override options
  • AI-powered product recommendations (WooCommerce)
  • Per-post sync and searchability controls

upgrade_notice.1.1.1: Adds WooCommerce HPOS and Cart/Checkout blocks compatibility declarations. Resolves the "incompatible plugins" warning.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: New [savanto_search] shortcode for placing a search trigger button anywhere on your site. Supports multiple variants, dark mode, and keyboard shortcuts.
upgrade_notice.1.0.8: Fixed sync cleanup bug that could delete valid cloud documents when plan limit is reached, and PHP 8 error handling fix.
upgrade_notice.1.0.7: Fixed orphan cleanup to respect post type filters during sync.
upgrade_notice.1.0.6: Fixed DELETE API requests to send request body correctly.
upgrade_notice.1.0.5: Improved cache invalidation and error handling for sync operations.
upgrade_notice.1.0.4: Moved inline CSS to enqueued stylesheet per WordPress coding standards.
upgrade_notice.1.0.3: Improved service status messaging and user-friendly sync error messages.
upgrade_notice.1.0.2: Fixed admin notice placement on plugin pages.
upgrade_notice.1.0.0: Initial release. Install Savanto to add AI powered search and chat to your WordPress site.

screenshots.caption: AI Chat Assistant – A knowledgeable shopping assistant on your storefront. Visitors ask natural questions and get personalized product recommendations with images and prices.
Semantic Search – Visitors search in their own words like "something elegant for a dinner party" and get relevant results. No exact keyword matching needed.
Instant Search Widget – As-you-type suggestions that understand meaning, surfacing the right products and content before visitors finish typing.
Smart Recommendations – "You may also like" suggestions on product pages, drawn from what the visitor is looking for rather than from a category list.
Live Agent Handoff – When the AI can't resolve a question, visitors are smoothly handed off to your human support team.
Dashboard Overview – Your Savanto workspace: products and content indexed, searches and chats today, and 30 day usage trends at a glance.
Usage Analytics – Track products indexed, content synced, daily searches, and chats with 30 day trends and a content breakdown.
Chat Analytics – Monitor conversations, visitor engagement, average messages, and feedback satisfaction scores with trend tracking.
Knowledge Base – View and manage all indexed products and content from the Savanto dashboard.
One-Click Connect – Connect a site without copying a key. Sign in or create a free account, approve the connection, and content starts syncing.
Connection Settings – Confirm which workspace a site is connected to, jump to the dashboard, or disconnect.
Content Sync – Choose which content Savanto can search and answer questions about. Posts, pages, and WooCommerce products are supported, with live sync status per type.
Taxonomies – Sync product categories, tags, brands, and custom taxonomies so visitors can filter and narrow search results.
Per-Post Controls – Sync and Visibility columns in the Posts, Pages and Products lists, so a single item can be excluded or hidden without leaving WordPress.
Theme Colors – Customize widget colors for light and dark modes. Use AI to generate a harmonious palette from your brand color.
Prompts Manager – Create suggested questions that appear in your chat widget to guide visitors toward common topics.
Live Agent Settings – Configure handoff to your human support team, including Slack integration for live agent requests.
API Keys – Manage secret and publishable API keys for custom integrations and advanced implementations.
